nodes.statement: The apparent flatness of N_c(w) for rigid families is an optimization artifact: small networks get stuck in local minima and fail to find the low-dimensional solution, making the problem appear "fat" (high capacity required) when it is actually rigid.

The capacity N_c(w) is governed by the covering number of the solution manifold in function space; for rigid (low-dimensional) manifolds, the covering number grows slowly with w, while for fat (high-dimensional) manifolds, it grows rapidly.

The rigidity of the solution space is linked to the connectivity of the loss landscape; rigid problems have a single connected basin of attraction, while fat problems have multiple disconnected basins, causing N_c(w) to increase as w samples force the network to navigate between them.
